As people approach retirement, they often begin to think about life after work, including how they will spend their time and manage the transition. This typically involves some degree of informal planning, such as considering finances, hobbies, or daily routines, even if not formalized. While absenteeism or anxiety might occur in some cases, they are not as consistently supported by research on retirement preparation as general, informal planning is.  

Final answer: (C)
